card: Bitcoin Core returns an empty HTTP 403 response when requests are refused by -rpcwhitelist, causing HTTP clients to show uninformative errors and causing bitcoin-cli over IPC to fail with JSON type errors. This PR updates whitelist denials to return JSON-RPC error bodies with new codes RPC_METHOD_NOT_PERMITTED (-38) and RPC_REQUEST_NOT_EXECUTED (-39). JSON-RPC 2.0 and batch requests receive HTTP 200 with structured errors, while legacy 1.x requests receive HTTP 403 with an error payload. The issue was identified in a private security audit of the IPC interface.
changed_since_previous: Added a fix in `bitcoin-cli -generate` to inspect the RPC error field in replies from `generatetoaddress` so permission denials exit with an error code instead of printing null block outputs, with accompanying functional test coverage.
evidence: "The empty reply causes a concrete problem when JSON-RPC requests are sent over IPC instead of HTTP: bitcoin-cli -ipcconnect receives only the response body, so a refused call prints a JSON type error instead of a permission error, as described in a private security review" (PR description)
doc/JSON-RPC-interface.md documents that JSON-RPC 2.0 requests report failed method calls as JSON-RPC errors rather than HTTP error codes (PR description, commit 2badf99744)
problem: When `-rpcwhitelist` rejects a call, Bitcoin Core returns an HTTP 403 with an empty body. For JSON-RPC 2.0 clients, this violates documented specifications requiring errors in the response body. For `bitcoin-cli -ipcconnect`, which transmits only the body over IPC without HTTP headers, this triggers confusing JSON type errors. Additionally, `bitcoin-cli -generate` does not check for errors returned by `generatetoaddress`, printing null results and exiting with success on failure.

risk.why: Alters HTTP status codes and response bodies for whitelist-rejected RPC requests and batches, which could break third-party clients expecting HTTP 403 responses.

scope_notes: Changes RPC error handling behavior for `-rpcwhitelist` denials: clients checking for HTTP 403 on JSON-RPC 2.0 or batch requests will now receive HTTP 200 with JSON-RPC error bodies. Moves connection fields from `JSONRPCRequest` to a new `JSONRPCClient` struct.
summary: Report `-rpcwhitelist` denials as structured JSON-RPC error responses instead of empty HTTP 403 replies. Introduce error codes `RPC_METHOD_NOT_PERMITTED` (-38) for refused calls and `RPC_REQUEST_NOT_EXECUTED` (-39) for other commands held back in a rejected batch. Refactor request parsing to split client connection state into `JSONRPCClient` and unify batch processing, and fix `bitcoin-cli -generate` to check for RPC errors before parsing results.
